judgments.reasoning_cat1: The preamble simply names the parties, the Effective Date and the Employee's address, and the operative sentence ('the Company agrees to employ ... on terms and conditions set forth below') has no term needing construction beyond OCR noise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fixes the contracting Company as Ajuba Solutions (India) Pvt Ltd, yet Section 7.5's notice address for the Company is Ajuba International, LLC/MiraMed in Michigan, Section 7.8 recites an integration 'between the Company, Parent and the Employee', and the whole of Section 2.4 hangs on MiraMed, an entity never identified — so who is bound is genuinely contestable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Business' is defined by an open-ended 'including but not limited to' list appended to the vague catch-all 'such other entities serviced by the Company at any time', a textbook general-vs-specific/ejusdem generis problem, and its geographic reach ('the United States and India') is bolted onto activities 'at any time during the Employment Term'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Business' feeds the Company Technology definition (1.2), the Confidential Information definition (1.3) and the assignment obligation (4.1), so its breadth propagates, but I found no provision that contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition sweeps in ideas 'patentable or unpatentable, copyrightable or non-copyrightable' merely 'known to the Employee as a result of or through' employment 'and which relate to the Business' — 'relate to' and 'known to' are undefined boundaries that could cover the Employee's pre-existing general knowledge.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 4.1 speaks of technology the Employee 'conceived, developed or acquired during the Employment Term', a narrower trigger than 1.2's 'known to the Employee', and 5.1 assumes he may hold prior proprietary-rights commitments; the two ownership triggers do not sit perfectly together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'All information, in whatever form, regarding the Company and the Business, and their clients' followed by a nine-item 'including, without limitation' list is precisely the general-catch-all-against-enumerated-specifics structure, and its literal breadth (any information at all) is unworkable without construction.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.1's carve-outs for public-domain and rightfully-received information cut back the definition, which harmonises rather than conflicts; no other provision contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Customer shall mean a client of the Company' defines one undefined word by another undefined word and gives no temporal or scope limit (present, past, prospective clients?).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: I grepped the whole instrument: 'Customer' is never used again — a defined term with no operative home, which suggests a non-solicitation covenant was dropped, and the same is true of 'Fiscal Year' (1.6) and 'Person' (1.7).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A fixed commencement (Effective Date) and a fixed end (December 31, 2013) with an express carve-out for earlier termination under Article 6 leaves nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It dovetails with Section 6.1(i) (termination at the end of the Employment Term) and with the severance measure in 6.4 (remainder of the Term); the only friction is that 6.1(ii) adds termination on a Liquidity Event, which the definition contemplates only via Article 6.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text as it survives reads 'the [twelve-]month period beginning on January 1', with the numeral dropped, and the alternative 'or such other 12-month period as may constitute the Company's fiscal year' is standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Fiscal Year' is never used anywhere else in the Agreement — an orphan definition, which is untidy but creates no operative conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition is truncated and ends on the general catch-all 'other entity or', so the residual class after 'corporation, company, partnership' is exactly the kind of open-ended term ejusdem generis is used on.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Person' appears nowhere else in the operative text, so it cannot conflict with anything; its orphan status only echoes the same drafting slippage seen with 'Customer'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The duty clauses turn on open-textured standards — duties 'as are customarily performed' by a President, 'full professional and business-related time, skills and best efforts', and a bar on engaging 'whether or not during normal business hours, in any other business or professional activity' — each of which two sides could read very differently in a competing-venture dispute.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cross-refers to Schedule 2.1, which is not part of the instrument, yet Section 6.2(b) makes failure to perform duties 'consistent with the provisions of Schedule 2.1' a Cause ground and Section 6.4 measures Good Reason by diminution of duties 'as outlined in Section 2.1' — the content of the duty is therefore located in a missing document.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Allowance is granted expressly 'in lieu of' health, dental and other benefits afforded to US employees of the Parent, while the following paragraph makes the Employee eligible for plans offered to employees generally 'subject to modification or discontinuance at the sole discretion of the Company' — the interaction of 'in lieu of' and the general eligibility sentence is genuinely readable two ways.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This is the only compensation section, yet it defines only 'Base Salary' and 'Allowance'; Sections 6.2, 6.3, 6.4 and 6.5 all promise 'Base Salary and Bonus' and no 'Bonus' is ever defined (the only use is the heading of 2.4, the Liquidity Event Bonus), leaving a hole the severance clauses cannot fill.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard reimbursement clause qualified by 'reasonable out-of-pocket expenses', 'in accordance with Company policies' and 'reasonably required' records — conventional and rarely litigated wording.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing in Article 6's payment-on-termination provisions or in Section 2.2 touches expense reimbursement, so it fits the instrument without friction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The three-tier formula is internally discontinuous (2.73% up to $180M, a flat US$5,000,000 to $200M, then 2.3% above $200M, so a larger Enterprise Value can yield a smaller payment), the phrase 'in lieu of any amounts otherwise payable to you on account of any prior agreements' is undefined as to which agreements, and payment is conditioned on a Separation Agreement 'in the form attached hereto' which is not attached.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The bonus requires the Employee to be 'employed by the Company at the time of consummation', yet Section 6.1(ii) provides that employment terminates 'upon the consummation of a Liquidity Event', and Section 2.4(d)'s deferred-payment condition compounds the circularity; Section 7.8's integration clause also supersedes the very 'prior agreements' this paragraph assumes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The paragraph twice cites 'Cause (as defined in Section 6.4 below)' when Cause is in fact defined in Section 6.2 — a cross-reference error visible on the face of the provision — and it gives a flat 1.75% with no tiering, unlike 2.4(a).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read against Sections 6.2 and 6.4, the mis-citation has to be corrected by construction, and the 1.75% figure sits awkwardly against the 2.73%/US$5,000,000/2.3% ladder in 2.4(a) and against the severance already payable under 6.4.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Limb (ii) crams three transactions together and the qualifier 'in which Tony Mira and members of his immediate family will not own at least 50% of the voting equity interests in the surviving entity' may modify only the merger or all three — a genuine syntactic ambiguity in a definition worth millions, and the (i)/(ii)/(iii) enumeration is itself mis-run.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The definition drives both the bonus in 2.4(a)-(b) and automatic termination of employment under 6.1(ii), and it turns entirely on 'MiraMed', an entity never defined or connected to the contracting Company (Ajuba Solutions (India) Pvt Ltd) anywhere in the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The valuation build-up ('plus, without duplication' indebtedness, repurchases, dividends and distributions) is broadly worded and the paragraph ends with an employment condition that has nothing to do with defining Enterprise Value, so the sentence is misplaced as well as open-ended.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its condition that a deferred Contingent Payout requires 'you remaining as an employee of the Company at the time that payment is due' cannot be squared with Section 6.1(ii), under which employment terminates upon consummation of the Liquidity Event, nor with 2.4(b), which pays a former employee.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The mechanics (Wall Street Journal rate, 10-trading-day average) are precise, but the paragraph repeatedly uses the capitalised term 'Transaction', which is nowhere defined in the Agreement, whereas 2.4(a)-(c) use 'Liquidity Event'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The undefined 'Transaction' must be read back onto 'Liquidity Event' in 2.4(c), a harmonisation a court could be asked to perform, though no provision positively contradicts the valuation mechanics.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The prohibition runs to disclosure 'to any entity' — literally omitting natural persons — and the exceptions (a)-(d) are an enumerated carve-out list whose last limb is truncated ('to the extent disclosure is [required]'), so both the prohibition's reach and the exceptions' scope invite argument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits on the 1.3 definition of Confidential Information and is reinforced by 3.2 and 7.7 (survival); the exceptions narrow rather than contradict the definition, so I found no true conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional return-and-delete obligation triggered by termination; the only softness is the undefined moment of 'termination of employment' and the extent of 'possession, custody or control'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It parallels 4.2 for Company Technology and depends on 1.3 and 3.1; nothing in Article 6 or 7.7 pulls against it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line covenant whose sole qualifier, 'except for legitimate business purposes', is a naked vagueness term with no boundary — it could swallow the obligation entirely and is the kind of phrase a court must construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the mirror of the Employee's confidentiality duty in 3.1, which has carefully enumerated exceptions; the asymmetry is odd but no provision directly contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard acknowledgement, return and delete-or-destroy obligation; the drafting is garbled by OCR but no term carries two reasonable meanings on its face.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A representation qualified by an enumerated (i)-(iii) list of subject matters with the exception 'except for this Agreement or as disclosed to the Company in writing'; the list is closed and the qualifier is specific.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps 5.2 and the acknowledgement in 7.8 that the Employee 'is not a party to any other employment agreement with the Company and/or its affiliates', which is consistent rather than contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional no-violation representation, fully sentenced and internally consistent, with an illustrative 'including, without limitation' reference to non-compete or confidentiality agreements with a former employer.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It complements 5.1 and 7.8 and breach of it is a Cause ground under 6.2(c); I found no provision it contradicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause purports to list every way employment ends but runs 'the first to occur of any of the events set forth in Sections 6.4 through 6.5', omitting termination for Cause (6.2) and for death or Disability (6.3) — an enumeration error visible on the face of the provision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Limb (ii), automatic termination 'upon the consummation of a Liquidity Event', cannot be reconciled with Section 2.4(a) (bonus payable only if 'employed by the Company at the time of consummation') or with 2.4(d) (deferred payment conditioned on 'remaining as an employee'), and its omission of 6.2 and 6.3 conflicts with those sections' express termination rights.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Cause' is defined by a run-on list containing genuinely elastic terms — 'conduct causing the Company or its subsidiaries substantial public disgrace or disrepute', 'misappropriation (which shall not include incidental personal use of supplies)' — and the fifteen-day 'opportunity to cure such failure' is ambiguous as to whether it attaches to every listed ground or only to the failure-to-perform ground.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It measures duties by 'Schedule 2.1 hereof', a schedule not part of the instrument, promises 'Base Salary and Bonus' when no 'Bonus' is defined anywhere, refers to 'state or federal laws' in an agreement whose tax clause (7.6) invokes only Indian law, and 6.1 does not list 6.2 as a termination trigger.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Disability' is given a numeric test (120 days in any 240) but qualified by 'substantially failed to perform his essential duties ... with or without reasonable accommodation', and the surviving text is fragmentary as to what Base Salary continues after a Disability termination.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It promises Base Salary 'but not any Bonus' for the remainder of the year although 'Bonus' is nowhere defined, and Section 6.1 omits 6.3 from its list of events on which employment terminates.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Good Reason' is defined by a list whose limbs are damaged and open-ended — 'a material diminution ... in the Employee's position, duties, authority, or responsibilities, as outlined in Section 2.1' and 'a breach by the Company of the compensation and benefit provisions' — with 'material' and 'diminution' both undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The severance measure is 'the Base Salary and Bonus' for the remainder of the Term, but no 'Bonus' is defined in Section 2.2 or elsewhere; the diminution test points to Section 2.1, whose content lives in the missing Schedule 2.1, and 2.4(b) layers a separate 1.75% payment on the same trigger.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: That 'allowed'/'required' divergence from 6.2 and 6.4 is a real inconsistency, and like those clauses it invokes 'state or federal laws' and an undefined 'Bonus' in a contract performed in India and taxed under Indian law per 7.6.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A boilerplate headings clause with a single, definite effect; no term in it carries competing meanings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It simply neutralises the section headings elsewhere (including the 'Liquidity Event Bonus' heading in 2.4) and contradicts nothing.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence, one rule: all payments are subject to withholding 'as required by Indian law'; nothing in it is capable of two readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It presupposes an Indian-law employment relationship while Sections 6.2, 6.4 and 6.5 condition benefit continuation on 'state or federal laws or regulations' (US concepts) and the Agreement has no governing-law clause at all, leaving a genuine whole-instrument mismatch.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 7.4 makes the Agreement binding on and inuring to the parties' heirs and personal representatives, and 6.3 contemplates payments in respect of the Employee's death, which sit uneasily with a flat ban on any alienation or transfer of benefits.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause protects each party's officers, directors 'or employers' — plainly a mistyping of 'employees', which changes the class protected — and 'disparage' is left undefined while the obligation runs 'during the Employment Term and thereafter', i.e. perpetually.
